subject: MSA + Order Form: IP handoff, feedback license, and evidence request
messages:
From: Sarah Mercer <sarah.mercer@quellhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@quellhealth.com>
Date: 2029-05-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form: IP questions on output ownership and training

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal and security teams reviewed the MSA and the draft order form and flagged a couple of items we need to resolve before procurement can finish onboarding. High level:

1) Output ownership: the draft language that assigns downstream productization rights to Redwood feels broad. We need explicit carveouts that preserve Quell Health ownership of patient-facing content generated from our proprietary prompts and PII-derived datasets.
2) Training/data use: we need clear confirmation that customer content will not be used to train models beyond the scope of the deployment without opt-in and that telemetry does not include PHI.
3) Feedback license: we understand the need for feedback for quality and safety, but we need a timebox and scope (non-identifiable, aggregated metrics only).

Can you provide: (a) a proposed set of order-form clauses that narrow the productization language; (b) an example of the telemetry and data artifacts Redwood might ingest; and (c) the compliance evidence you can share (SOC2, DLP posture) so our security folks can sign off?

We attached the redlined MSA excerpt from our counsel for reference.

Appreciate quick turnaround—our board is pushing a June 1 launch.

Best,
Sarah Mercer
Head of Platform, Quell Health
[sarah.mercer@quellhealth.com]

Attachments: Quell_MSA_redlines_20290503.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mercer <sarah.mercer@quellhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@quellhealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-03T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: IP questions on output ownership and training

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Short answers up front: we can tighten the output/productization language with a customer-first carveout, implement an explicit training opt-in, and limit feedback ingestion to non-PII aggregated telemetry with a 12-month retention cap unless you opt in to longer retention.

What I'll do next:
- Share a proposed order-form supplement that narrows the productization clause and adds an explicit "Customer Output" definition that excludes Quell proprietary prompts/data.
- Include a short example of telemetry artifacts (redacted sample) so your security team can see what we actually collect.
- Provide SOC2 Type II report excerpt and a short note on our DLP/KMS posture.

I've attached the redlined orderform v3 we intend to propose to legal (redlined_orderform_v3.docx). Connor, can you review the proposed carveouts below and confirm operational feasibility?

Proposed carveouts (draft language snippets):
- "Customer Output": any model output that is the direct transcription, transformation, or synthesis of Customer Proprietary Data. Customer retains exclusive rights to Customer Output for productization and downstream commercialization.
- Training Opt-In: Customer Data will not be used to train or refine models for any third-party or shared model variants without explicit, documented opt-in administered via the Console or signed amendment.
- Feedback License Scope: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated, de-identified feedback for internal model quality and safety improvements for a period not to exceed 12 months from collection, unless mutually extended.

If that aligns, we'll send a formal order-form amendment plus the compliance docs by end of day.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
